about: HIGH and CRITICAL advisories against the runtime dependency tree of echelongraph-mcp that a release ships with, each reviewed, with why and until when. scripts/npm-publish-mcp.sh's preflight (its dry run and --publish) resolves the packed tarball's production dependencies afresh, runs npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high on them, and refuses every HIGH or CRITICAL advisory not accepted here (#3382). An entry has exactly these fields: advisory (its GHSA id, as npm audit's URL names it), package (the package npm audit names it against), reason (why the release can ship with it, at least 20 characters), reviewed (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, the day it was reviewed) and expires (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, the last day it accepts, at most 90 days after reviewed). From the day after expires, the entry refuses every release, whether npm audit still finds the advisory or not, until it is reviewed again (a new reviewed and expires) or removed, in a reviewed commit. MODERATE and lower advisories are printed, never refused, and need no entry. scripts/npm-publish-mcp.sh --check-runtime-advisories reads this list too, for the tarball npm serves as latest, and exits 1 on an advisory it does not accept and on an expired entry. Empty on 2026-10-29: the tree of echelongraph-mcp 3.1.2, npm's latest, and of mcp-server/ at this commit (@modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.0, its core 2.3.0, zod 4.6.6) has no advisory npm audit names.
